answers.question: A reviewer found that a rule adds a case you did not give. The rule now says, after a refund call that timed out and its one retry: "the read fails, it says the refund's status is unknown and hands the case to staff. When that read fails but the retry answered pending or issued, the agent tells the customer what the retry answered." I propose to delete the second sentence, so that a failed read always leads to "status unknown" and a hand-off to staff, as you said. What it leads to: the refund call times out; the agent sends it once more and that call answers issued; the agent reads the refund again and the read fails; the agent tells the customer the refund's status is unknown and hands the case to staff as refund status unknown. This also covers a retry that answered another amount: the case goes to staff as refund status unknown. Do you accept the change?
answers.recommended: Yes: delete the sentence; when the read after the retry fails, the agent says the status is unknown and hands the case to staff.
answers.reply: > For case 3, after the retry the agent re-reads the refund record: pending or issued, report that status; failed or no refund, hand off and say the refund is not confirmed yet; re-read fails, say status unknown and hand off.

answers.question: The rule on which order to cancel covers only two open orders. Before: "When the customer has two open orders and does not say which one to cancel, the agent asks which one and proposes nothing until the customer names it." After: "When the customer has more than one open order and does not say which one to cancel, the agent asks which one and proposes nothing until the customer names it." Do you accept the change?
answers.recommended: Yes: the agent asks which order whenever the customer has more than one open order and does not say which.
answers.reply:
Yes, I accept your recommendation.
> 1. Wrong order cancelled — customer has two open orders and says "cancel my order"; agent must disambiguate and get a confirmation naming the order number before the cancel call.

answers.question: Two rules give the customer different messages for an order that shipped after the yes, and one leaves out a delivered order. Before, first rule: "When the cancel call answers that the order is not cancellable, or the order read again shows it shipped, the agent says the order can no longer be cancelled and issues no refund." After: "When the cancel call answers that the order is not cancellable, or the order read again shows it shipped or delivered, the agent says the order can no longer be cancelled, issues no refund, and tells the customer returns are a separate process." Before, second rule (after a cancel call with no answer and the order read again): "Shipped, it says the order can no longer be cancelled and issues no refund." After: "Shipped or delivered, it says the order can no longer be cancelled, issues no refund, and tells the customer returns are a separate process." Do you accept both changes?
answers.recommended: Yes to both: for an order that shipped or was delivered after the yes, the agent says it can no longer be cancelled, issues no refund, and says returns are a separate process.
answers.reply:
Yes, I accept your recommendation.
> Recommended: only orders that have not shipped yet; for a shipped or delivered order the agent says it cannot cancel and changes nothing; returns are a separate future capability.
> Once shipped, the agent refuses without issuing a cancel call and tells the customer returns are a separate process (out of scope for v1).
> Note the race: status can flip processing → shipped between the agent's read and its cancel call; the store rejects the cancel and the agent must report that truthfully and issue no refund call.
> Shipped, report it and issue no refund.
> Outcomes: cancelled; OrderNotCancellable{status} (replaces OrderShipped, covers shipped and delivered); OrderNotFound; timeout.
